title: How to Stream on Riftn: Every Way to Go Live, Step by Step
html:
Riftn gives you nine ways to go live, and they all land on the same profile, the same followers and the same chat. Pick the one that fits your setup, follow the steps below, and you can be live in under a minute.

This guide covers every way in, then every tool that makes a stream better: Live Studio, the chat bot, channel points, badges, tips, clips and more. Every screenshot is from the real Riftn app and website.

Every way to go live at a glance

  1. Camera from your computer, phone browser or the Riftn app.
  2. Screen share from a desktop browser or the Riftn app.
  3. OBS or any encoder with one permanent stream key.
  4. Capture card straight from a desktop browser, no OBS needed.
  5. Stages for live audio rooms.
  6. Guests on your live, or a gift battle with another creator.
  7. Group calls with live subtitles.
  8. Multistream to Twitch, YouTube, Kick and more.
  9. Live Studio to run alerts, widgets and your chat.

Before you start

  1. Join free at riftn.com, or get the Riftn app for Android or iPhone. Sign in with Google, Apple, email, a passkey or a wallet.
  2. Pick a username and a profile picture, so people know who is live.
  3. Allow your camera and microphone when your browser or phone asks.

Way 1: Go live with your camera on desktop

  1. Click Post to open the composer.
  2. Click the live icon in the bottom toolbar. A small menu opens.
  3. Pick Camera.
  4. Type a title. Add a description and a cover image if you like.
  5. Click Go Live. Riftn creates your live post and puts it in the feed.

Want to go live later? Open the Livestream tab at the top of the composer and press Schedule livestream. Your followers get a post they can share before you start.

Big event is a switch on the Go Live sheet for large audiences. Viewers watch about 20 seconds behind you, with fewer interruptions.

Your browser studio

Once you are live in the browser, the broadcast panel works like a small studio:

  • Scenes: Starting soon (with a countdown), Just chatting, Gameplay, Be right back (mic muted) and Stream ending.
  • Background: blur it, swap it for a colour or use a picture. It runs on your own device.
  • Sources: add a logo, a second camera, a video clip, or react to any Riftn video.
  • Audio mixer: balance your mic, game or tab sound and clips. A noise gate keeps keyboard clicks off stream.
  • Guests: bring people on screen with you (see Way 6).

Way 2: Share your screen

  1. Open the composer, click the live icon and pick Camera, or open the Go Live sheet.
  2. Under How do you want to stream?, pick Screen.
  3. Choose the screen, window or browser tab to share.
  4. Press Go Live. Riftn sends your screen with your mic and the tab's own sound.

Phone browsers do not let any website share the screen. On a phone, go live from the Riftn app and tap Share screen instead.

Way 3: Stream from OBS, Streamlabs or any encoder

Use this for pro setups, game consoles and saved scene collections.

  1. Open the composer, click the live icon and pick OBS / Encoder.
  2. Copy your Ingest URL and Stream Key.
  3. In OBS, open Settings, then Stream, and set Service to Custom.
  4. Paste the Ingest URL into Server and the key into Stream Key.
  5. Press Start Streaming in OBS. Riftn creates the live post for you.

Your key never changes, so you only do this once. Next time, just press Start in OBS. Keep the key secret, because anyone with it can stream to your account.

In the Riftn app, the same key is behind Stream from OBS or another encoder on the go-live screen.

Way 4: Use a capture card without OBS

Got an Elgato, AVerMedia or another capture card for your console or camera?

  1. Plug it into your computer.
  2. In the composer's live menu, pick Capture card.
  3. Choose the card, check the preview and press Go Live.

Capture cards work from a desktop browser only, because phones cannot take a USB capture card.

Way 5: Go live from the Riftn app

  1. Tap + and choose Live.
  2. Add a title, then tap Go Live.
  3. On the camera screen, flip the camera, mute the mic, turn the camera off or open Camera looks for filters.
  4. Tap Studio for scenes, background blur, an image or logo, and widgets drawn into your video.
  5. Tap Go Live. While you are live, tap Share screen to show your phone screen instead.

Screen share in the app needs the latest version from the App Store or Google Play.

Way 6: Bring guests on screen or start a gift battle

When you are live from the browser, open Guests:

  1. Press Open guest seats.
  2. Invite by username, or Copy invite link and send it.
  3. Switch on Let viewers ask to join. Requests show under Asking to join, and you press Bring on screen.
  4. Up to 3 guests can be on screen with you. Ask guests to wear headphones so they do not hear themselves back.

Want a challenge? Press Find a co-streamer. Riftn pairs you with another creator who is live right now for a Gift battle. Each side scores the gifts its own stream gets during the round, and both audiences see the bar.

Way 7: Host a Stage, a live audio room

Stages are live audio rooms for talk shows, Q&As, music and watch parties.

  1. Open the composer and pick the Stages tab, or go to riftn.com/stages and press Start a Stage.
  2. Add a title and press Go live now, or press Schedule stage to announce it with a cover graphic people can share.
  3. Listeners raise a hand under Requests to Speak. Tap + to invite them up as a speaker.
  4. Add your own music clips and they play to the room one after another, like a radio station.

Want a music show? Switch on Radio show when you start the Stage. It plays your own songs or a playlist, you talk when you like, listeners drop in any time, and your show appears in the Radio row on Explore.

Every Stage is recorded. When it ends, people can listen back, read the transcript, search it and translate it.

Stages also speak every language. Listeners can turn on Subtitles in their own language. Hosts can record a fifteen-second voice sample once, and listeners who turn on dubbing hear the Stage in their language, in the host's own voice.

Way 8: Start a group call

  1. Open a group chat.
  2. Tap Start a group voice call or Start a group video call. Everyone in the group gets a ring.
  3. People who missed the ring tap Join call.
  4. Tap Subtitles to read what everyone says, translated into your language.
  5. In a video call, tap Effects to blur your room, pick a scene like Night, Ocean, Sunset or Forest, use Your photo as the background, or add a face filter like Shades, Cat, Crown or Hearts.

Group admins choose who can start calls in the group's settings.

Way 9: Multistream to every platform for free

Go live on Riftn once, and Riftn pushes your stream to every platform you switch on.

  1. Open Live Studio.
  2. Under Multistream destinations, press Add destination.
  3. Pick Twitch, YouTube, Kick, X, Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, LinkedIn or Custom RTMP.
  4. Paste the server and stream key that platform gives you. Riftn stores your key encrypted and never shows it again.
  5. Switch on the destinations you want. They start a few seconds after you go live.

Set up Live Studio

Live Studio is your control room. Open it from the Go Live sheet, from the app's menu or at riftn.com/live-studio. Everything you set up works however you go live: phone, browser, capture card or OBS.

Widgets and alerts

  1. Press Add widget and pick from tip, follow, subscriber, share and join alerts, a goal bar, top supporters, a viewer count, a chat box, a ticker, a poll, a spin wheel, a subathon timer, a hype train, a gift jar and more. You can add up to 40.
  2. Drag each widget into place on the Preview. Landscape and portrait streams keep their own layout.
  3. Press Test alerts to see them. Only you see test alerts.
  4. Choose where they show: In the Riftn app, drawn by each viewer's app, or In my video, burned into your picture so they appear on Twitch and YouTube too.
  5. Using OBS? Copy the Browser source link into an OBS Browser source at 1920 by 1080.

Everything else in Live Studio

  • Quick controls: pause alerts, mute alert sounds or stop read-aloud mid-stream.
  • Vertical view: drag a box to choose what phones see in the vertical feed.
  • Polls: viewers vote with a button in the app, or by typing !vote and a number in chat.
  • Subathon: a countdown that gifts, follows and subscriptions push back.
  • Channel points rewards: set up to 12 rewards viewers spend points on, like "Hydrate!" or "Pick the next song".
  • Loyal viewers: your top viewers by points.
  • Limited-time badges: offer a badge for a few days to everyone who subscribes or gifts.
  • Rules: when a tip, follow, subscription, share or chat command happens, show an alert, play a sound, read it aloud, post in chat, spin a wheel or ping Discord.
  • Chat moderation: slow mode, followers-only or subscribers-only chat, banned words, moderators and bans.
  • Highlights and clips: moments where chat or gifts spike are clipped for you. Approve one to post it to Shorts.

Turn on the chat bot

The chat bot is a co-host for your stream chat. It is off until you switch it on.

  1. In Live Studio, open Chat bot and switch it on.
  2. Fill in What it knows about you: who you are, what you stream and your schedule.
  3. Pick a Personality (Chill, Hype, Funny or Formal) and How chatty it is.
  4. Choose what it does: say hi to first-time chatters, answer questions, catch up late joiners with "What did I miss?", wake up a quiet chat, and show your !commands as tap buttons above the chat box.

It posts as @assistant, only on your own streams while you are live. It never talks about money or tokens, and never makes promises for you. If it does not know an answer, it stays quiet.

Add your own commands under Rules with the trigger A chat command is used, for example !schedule or !discord.

How viewers back you

  • Tips and gifts: viewers pick a celebration, from Love Heart and Box of Chocolate up to Golden Screen and Ultimate Celebration. They can add a message that is read aloud. Tips go straight to your wallet, on chain.
  • Subscriptions and gift subs: fans subscribe to your plans, or gift subs to people in your chat.
  • Hype train: three gifts or subscriptions within five minutes start one. Everyone who rides it earns your 🚂 badge.
  • Channel points: viewers earn a point for every minute they watch, plus one for every 100 tokens they gift. Chat and reactions earn nothing, so points cannot be farmed. Points have no cash value.
  • Giving points: turn on Let viewers give channel points in Live Studio and viewers can tap a name in your live chat to give that person some of their points. You set Most one viewer can give a day, so nobody can farm points onto one account.
  • Milestone badges: regulars earn a badge beside their name for watch time (1 hour up to 500 hours) and chat messages (10 up to 5K) on your streams.
  • Clip this moment: anyone can clip your stream from its three-dot menu. The clip posts as a Short that credits you.
  • Share: the share button reposts, quotes, sends in a message or copies the link without leaving the player.
  • Shop: put products from your store on stream, and viewers buy without leaving.
  • Picture in picture: viewers keep watching while they scroll.

After your stream

  • Stream recap: see time live, the most people watching at once, gifts, new followers, chat messages, top supporters and poll winners. Press Share to post it.
  • Replay: your stream stays on your profile as a replay. Free accounts keep the first part of each stream, and staking badges raises the limit.
  • Highlights: review the clips Live Studio found and post the best to Shorts.
  • Streamer level: streams of ten minutes or more with at least one viewer count toward your level, your weekly streak and collectible cards like First light, Marathon and Night owl.

Tips for a great first stream

  1. Test first. Use Test alerts in Live Studio and check your sound before you start.
  2. Schedule it. A scheduled post gives followers time to show up.
  3. Use a starting soon scene with a countdown while people arrive.
  4. Switch on the chat bot so nobody waits for a reply.
  5. Add three rewards so viewers have a reason to stay and earn points.
  6. Multistream to reach the audience you already have elsewhere.
  7. Share the recap when you finish.

Coming from Twitch or TikTok? Read Web3 live streaming: a decentralised Twitch alternative, then see how Riftn compares in the best decentralized streaming apps. Ready to start? Open riftn.com/stream.

FAQ

Is it free to stream on Riftn?

Yes. Going live, Stages, group calls, multistreaming and Live Studio are all free.

Can I stream on Riftn with OBS?

Yes. Pick OBS / Encoder in the live menu to get a permanent Ingest URL and Stream Key for OBS, Streamlabs or any RTMP encoder.

Can I share my screen from my phone?

Yes, in the Riftn app. Phone browsers do not allow screen sharing for any website, so use the app and tap Share screen.

Can I stream to Twitch and YouTube at the same time?

Yes. Add them under Multistream destinations in Live Studio, and Riftn sends your stream to every destination you switch on.

Can I go live with only audio?

Yes. Start a Stage for a live audio room with speakers, listeners, music, a recording and a transcript.

How do I get paid while I stream?

Viewers send tips and gifts during your stream, and they land in your wallet on chain. Fans can also subscribe or gift subscriptions.
